summary.headline: Ather's FY26 volumes rose ~66% with Q4 at 83,000 units; Q4 EBITDA loss narrowed to about -2% of revenue, while commodity inflation is expected to pressure margins near term.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a breakthrough year, with volumes up about 66% led by Rizta (almost three-quarters of sales) and market share up from about 8% to 18.6% in Q4. Store count doubled from 351 to 700 by March 2026, and AGM with subsidy improved from 19% to 24% (about 12% to 21% without subsidy) on COGS reduction of about 9 percentage points. Q4 EBITDA loss improved about 2,000 bps to roughly -2%. Management flagged sharp commodity inflation (lithium, rare earth magnets, memory, aluminium) that will pressure margins in the short term, with only a small part passed on so far, and said the Factory 3.0 (AURIC) and EL platform are the key FY27 levers.

financial_highlights.change: up ~23% QoQ per analyst question/management reference to volume growth
highest ever; rose through the year

segments.name: Middle India (Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, MP, Odisha, Maharashtra)
segments.commentary: Market share rose from about 4% at start of FY25 to 17.3%; store additions up 125% YoY. Gujarat and Odisha at about 19-20%, Maharashtra at 16%+ from about 8%.

segments.name: South India
segments.commentary: Market share moved from 13% to 23% with 80% more stores; quarterly sales rose from about 27,000 to about 41,000 units. Kerala Pro-Pack attach about 98-99%.

segments.name: Rest of India
segments.commentary: Market share tripled from just under 4% to about 12%; Rest of India Pro-Pack attach at 81%, the weakest zone.

guidance_outlook: EL platform (mass and mass-premium focus, INR1-1.25 lakh segment where Ather has no product) to be commercialised by festive season and in the field before end of CY26; management said no exact launch month given.

Factory 3.0 (AURIC, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar): Phase 1 of 5 lakh units capacity (10 lakh total) to start trial production before end CY26 and 42,000 units/month incremental capacity fully operational before end FY27; first revenue from new factory expected in Q4 FY27.
Cost reduction to come mainly from EL over FY27 (more back-loaded); 450/Rizta platform cost reduction to be smaller than prior two years.

Short-term margin pressure expected from commodity inflation (commodity cost inflation estimated at 40-50%, BOM increase a fraction of that); further price hike possible in coming months after roughly INR4,000 blended hikes in CY26 so far.
FAME subsidy expiry in coming months to reduce realisation by about INR5,000 per vehicle.
No specific new-store guidance for FY27; management expects the current quarterly EC opening pace to broadly continue.
capex_capacity: Current Hosur plant designed for 35,000 units/month; running at 90-95% utilisation for multiple recent months, with some headroom left.
AURIC Factory 3.0 Phase 1: 5 lakh capacity out of 10 lakh planned; adds 42,000 units/month; trial production before end CY26.
Factory 3.0 to add in-house battery pack assembly, transmission assembly, painting, electronics assembly and CED coating, raising vertical integration.
Hosur plant moved to triple-shift operation, adding depreciation.
Service centres more than doubled in FY26; store count doubled to 700.
demand_pricing: Q4 retail demand ran above estimates (retail includes units sold by dealers pending registration); supply rather than demand was the binding constraint.
Price hikes: about INR1,000-1,500 in Q4 FY26 and about INR2,500 blended in April 2026, roughly INR4,000 in CY26 so far.
Q4 ASP flat QoQ; management attributed this to Q4 offer structures and newer stores in Middle/North India, expecting it to rise as stores mature.
Pro-Pack attach: Kerala about 98-99%, Middle India second, Rest of India 81%; Madhya Pradesh rose from 40-50% to over 80-85% within about a year.
Lithium up about 2-2.5x from around $8/kg to about $24/kg at peak, cooled somewhat; cell share of BOM rose from 15-16% (sub-20%) to a larger share.
Competition: peers have many variants across price bands while Ather has 6 premium, 3 mass-premium and no mass or entry variants.
Industry: management views the sub-INR1 lakh segment as 15-20% of market, INR1.25 lakh and above as 25-30% (top-five-OEM volumes only, indicative).

qa_highlights.question: How do Pro-Pack attach rates differ between mature South markets and newer Middle/Rest of India markets?
qa_highlights.answer: South highest (Kerala ~98-99%), then Middle India, then Rest of India at 81%; new cities start lower and reach 80%+ within two to four quarters, with existing dealer partners ramping faster (about three-quarters of new stores).

qa_highlights.question: Is 400 branch expansion in FY27 accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific FY27 store guidance; EL is the main FY27-28 growth driver and store expansion is becoming business-as-usual at the current quarterly pace.

qa_highlights.question: How much commodity cost inflation has been passed on, and how will it be shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Only a small part passed on so far due to procurement and stockpiling; some burden may be shared with suppliers, but the bulk is expected to fall on the company or customer.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 ASP flat QoQ despite the price hike and higher attach rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q4 offer structures and newer stores in Middle and North India with lower ASPs, expecting these to normalise as stores age.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 34% and depreciation rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose on variable warranty and logistics costs with volume up, plus marketing and a year-end warranty calibration; depreciation reflects the 450 platform (seven-year life), triple-shift operation at Hosur, and useful-life recalibration of tools; EL amortisation starts next FY.

qa_highlights.question: Are there supply issues compared with competitors and when will new capacity contribute revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Only localised constraints (Nov-Dec variants, April election-related labour disruption); no secular material shortage. New factory revenue expected in Q4 FY27.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (lithium, aluminium, rare earths, memory) with management expecting margin pressure in the short term and limited pass-through so far.
EL launch timing (festive season or by end CY26) and Factory 3.0 Phase 1 commissioning slipping beyond CY26 / Q3 FY27.
FAME subsidy expiry removing about INR5,000 per vehicle from realisations in coming months.
Supply constraints at 90-95% utilisation of current plant limiting volume capture in South and Middle India.
Rising warranty provisions and variable other expenses; depreciation step-up as EL amortisation begins next FY.
Electric motorcycles would need a separate Zenith platform; no timeline given.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, market share and EBITDA progress, but cautious on near-term margins, saying commodity inflation will pressure margins and cannot be fully mitigated. Management avoided giving exact dates or FY27 store guidance, pointing to EL and Factory 3.0 timelines as directional.
key_quotes: Which means there will be a pressure on margins, one that we will try and mitigate as much as possible with price hikes and even more work on things like accessories and software, but they can't be fully mitigated.
So, we're definitely running at the edge, and hence any gaps are very unforgiving.
We're not giving any specific guidance for new store expansion in FY '27.
And the full 42,000 should be operationalized before end of this FY for sure.

adds.what: AURIC Factory 3.0 Phase 1: 5 lakh units capacity (10 lakh total), adds 42,000 units/month incremental

growth.why: Management guides growth via AURIC Factory 3.0 Phase 1 (+42,000 units/month, trial production before end CY26, fully operational before end FY27), EL platform commercialisation by festive/CY26, and share gains (18.6% Q4 share, FY26 volumes up ~66%), but gives no numeric revenue guidance and the Hosur plant is already at 90-95% utilisation.
